title: Peroxide-Templated Assembly of a Trimetal Neodymium Complex Single-Molecule Magnet

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: peroxide-templated trinuclear neodymium chloride complex of bis(2-pyridinal)ethylenediimine

material_class.structural_family: triangular Nd3 cluster with a central μ3-η2:η2:η2 peroxide

synthesis.procedure: Synthesized by azeotropic distillation open to air. NdCl3·6H2O (1.00 g, 2.7 mmol) was dissolved in absolute ethanol (20 mL). Bis(2-pyridinal)ethylenediamine (1.337 g, 5.4 mmol; 1:2 Nd:ligand) was dissolved in toluene (40 mL) and added. The mixture was distilled, removing the toluene/ethanol/water azeotrope at 74.4 °C, the ethanol/toluene azeotrope at 76.7 °C, and toluene at 110 °C. After all solvent was removed, a brown solid formed. It was redissolved in chloroform; continued air exposure precipitated a light-brown solid, recovered by centrifugation and chloroform washing and purified by recrystallization from methanol/pentane. Single crystals grew over 3 weeks by slow vapor diffusion of methanol and pentane at 0 °C.
synthesis.temperature: azeotrope removal at 74.4 °C, then 76.7 °C, then toluene at 110 °C; crystallization at 0 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: azeotropic distillation apparatus, open to air/oxygen; centrifugation; slow vapor diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Brown solid redissolved in chloroform; air exposure gave a light-brown precipitate recovered by centrifugation with chloroform washing, recrystallized from methanol/pentane, then crystallized by methanol/pentane vapor diffusion at 0 °C for 3 weeks.

properties.summary: SQUID data show paramagnetic-like susceptibility with overlapping zero-field-cooled and field-cooled curves, no long-range ferro- or antiferromagnetic order, and no hysteresis or remanence down to 5 K. A nonlinear M–H curve at 5 K fits the Langevin function, which the authors interpret as superparamagnetism from weakly interacting ferromagnetic Nd3 clusters and therefore single-molecule-magnet behavior, with blocking temperature much lower than 5 K. Room-temperature χT is 66.05 cm3 K mol−1, close to three free Nd3+ ions (61.5 cm3 K mol−1). The fitted cluster moment is 3.49 μB and the cluster density is 1.25×10^21 cm−3.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: mononuclear aqua neodymium chloride complex of bis(2-pyridinal)ethylenediimine

material_class.structural_family: mononuclear eight-coordinate Nd complex with one tetradentate diimine, one chloride, and aqua ligands

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by ligand exchange during azeotropic distillation with limited oxygen exposure. In a 100 mL round-bottom flask, NdCl3·6H2O (0.20 g, 0.4 mmol) was dissolved in absolute ethanol (10 mL). Bis(2-pyridinal)ethylenediamine (0.14 g, 0.4 mmol) in anhydrous toluene (30 mL) was added. The mixture was heated so that the toluene/ethanol/water azeotrope boiled at 74.4 °C, the ethanol/toluene azeotrope at 76.7 °C, and toluene at 110 °C. Complete solvent removal gave a brown solid, purified by recrystallization from methanol/pentane. Single crystals grew by slow methanol/pentane vapor diffusion for two weeks at 0 °C. The main text only notes that reduced oxygen exposure instead yields this monometallic hydrate and refers further detail to the Supporting Information.
